stories.headline: Government announces 115 billion kroner increase in defense spending through 2036
stories.summary: Prime Minister Støre unveiled an updated long-term defense plan adding 115 billion kroner to military spending by 2036, citing increased security threats. The plan prioritizes faster procurement of frigates, submarines, and drone capabilities while delaying some air defense systems.

stories.headline: Parliament overrides government with fuel tax cuts as Senterpartiet breaks ranks
stories.summary: The Stortinget voted to cut fuel taxes against the government's wishes after Senterpartiet joined with opposition parties Høyre, FrP and KrF. The move removes road usage taxes on diesel and gasoline temporarily, costing around 6.7 billion kroner and creating a budget crisis.

stories.headline: Norges Bank holds interest rates at 4% but signals potential increases amid inflation concerns
stories.summary: Central bank governor Ida Wolden Bache kept the key rate unchanged at 4% but warned of possible rate hikes later in 2026 due to persistently high inflation and geopolitical tensions. The bank revised upward its rate path, suggesting 1-2 rate increases by year-end.
